native_name: Naval Group SA (DCN Developpement, DCN, DCNS); predecessor the state directorate DCN

selection.reason: The French naval shipbuilder. It covers the naval side of the mix and is the clearest case where a state directorate (1990-2003) must not be turned into government production capacity when a company identity is attached.

existing_game_references.note: Generic escort kit built through public manufacturing lines; no company ship flow exists.

summary: In 1990 naval construction was a directorate of the Ministry of Defence (DCN), which became a national-competence service in 2000. A company, DCN Developpement, was created on 28 February 2002 and received the directorate's industrial rights, assets and obligations on 1 June 2003; it operated as DCN. On 29 March 2007 Thales contributed its naval activities, took 25% and the company became DCNS; Thales rose to 35% in 2011. The register shows the name NAVAL GROUP from 2017. The Suffren SSN was delivered in 2020, the first FDI frigate in 2025, and Australia's Attack-class programme was terminated in 2021.

proposed.uncertainty: Frigates exist only as the generic escort arsenal kit built through public manufacturing lines. There is no ship designer platform or company ship stock before E04; a future ship supplier must not be modeled as government production capacity or a free fleet.
The strategic-deterrent kit is a generic force tier. SSBN work in 1993-2003 belonged to a state directorate, not to a company.
Generated contractors are fictional; a real identity would replace one, not add a parallel firm.

duplicates_avoided: The DCN directorate (1990-2003) and the company (from 2002/2003) are separate records; the directorate is never a company or a production line owner in the game.
Thales is a shareholder and contributor, not a predecessor name of Naval Group.

integration_flow.summary: A later, reviewed integration could attach this sourced identity to a company created through the existing orders. Design stays with the commissioning country; Defense R&D pays development as work is performed; the company funds tooling, national-warehouse inputs and fabrication from its own settled cash; the buyer purchases whole finished units from company stock; delivery follows fiscal settlement and seven accessible days. Ships have no designer platform, company stock or delivery consumer today; naval use waits for E04 and must still avoid state production capacity.

steps.note: Paid capitalisation from Defense procurement (political capital price applies); leases one existing completed Arms Plant slot. No historical factory, balance or stock is granted.
Further paid working capital; unsettled receivables are not spendable cash.
Frozen design revision; Defense R&D pays engineering, prototype and trials work day by day; prototypes are never saleable.
Finite company-owned stock target (0-12 units); a target is never a government order.
Government buys whole units from existing company stock; settlement then seven accessible delivery days.

unmapped: Suffren-class SSN: no suitable kit; la_ssn is the US Los Angeles class and must not be relabelled.
Scorpene exports: aip_ssk would be wrong for the Chilean boats; no air-independent propulsion is sourced here.

gaps: DCN International creation date conflicts: the Naval Group history says 1991 (fr_naval_history_en), while the 2005 Senate report says the early 1970s (fr_senat_r04_405). Neither date is used.
The exact day of the DCN Developpement to DCN name change in 2003 was not found; the 2011 ministry answer names DCN Developpement at 1 June 2003.
The register records the NAVAL GROUP name by 12 October 2017 (still D C N S on 26 August 2017); announcement-day press coverage is a lead only.
La Cour des comptes website was unreachable; its findings were read only as reproduced in the Senate report.

future_policy.note: Nothing after the frozen cutoff is predicted. Any later product, successor or business in a campaign must be authored as explicitly fictional game content (labelled "(fictional)") or left unknown.
